brief.situation: 10:00 at an outpatient cardiac rehabilitation program. You are the physical therapist. Mr. Grant, 63, is 12 days after coronary artery bypass surgery through a sternotomy. At intake his wife says she 'pulls him up by both arms' to get him out of bed, and he plans to lift his 30-pound grandson this weekend. He mentions the bottom of his incision 'weeps a bit more' and he felt hot last night. He quit smoking the day of surgery.
handover: The surgeon's discharge sheet lists breastbone precautions for 6 weeks and when to call.
Program policy: wound or fever concerns go to the surgeon's office the same day; no exercise session until cleared.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What do you do first for Mr. Grant, and what do he and his wife need to learn?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: A red, swollen incision with more drainage and a fever over 101°F (38.3°C) is on the call-the-surgeon list: no exercise today. They also don't know the breastbone precautions: no pulling on his arms, nothing over 5 to 7 pounds.
parts.modelAnswer: His wound looks infected and he has a fever, so the surgeon today and no exercise. And neither of them knows not to pull on his arms or lift the grandson.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Call the surgeon's office now; teach them both with teach-back (getting out of bed without arm pulling, lifting limits, when to call); start smoking cessation, diet and stress support; document.
parts.modelAnswer: Call the surgeon, teach them both and have them show it back, set up smoking, diet and stress help, and write it up.

scoring.modelReasoning: Education is for the patient and family, and teach-back shows whether it landed. After sternotomy, for 6 weeks: no one pulls on his arms, no lifting over 5 to 7 pounds, no reaching back or overhead, and stop if the breastbone pulls. A changing wound (red, swollen, more drainage) or fever over 101°F (38.3°C) means calling the surgeon, so check before exercise. Risk-factor work (smoking cessation, nutrition, stress and mood) runs through every phase of rehab.

callQ.ask: While they get ready: which fever means calling the surgeon?
callQ.explain: Call for chills or a fever over 101°F (38.3°C), or a red, swollen, opened or more draining wound.
